title: Design: Activate part confirmation looks as in the design
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an inactive part for this test, part A.
  • Make sure the app is in the Light theme.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1600 pixels wide with the page zoom at 100%, so the screen is as wide as the design boards.
  • Open the attached design picture of board 3.7 at 100% zoom, so you can compare the screen with it.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Inactive tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part A row.
  3. Click Active under Part Status.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Click Cancel in the confirmation.
  6. Click Cancel.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part A is listed on the Inactive tab.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens with a grey "Inactive" pill.

Step 3:

  • The Active radio is filled blue and the pill still reads "Inactive".

Step 4:

  • A white dialog titled "Activate part?" opens over the dimmed window.
  • Its first line reads part A's part number, a space, then part A's description.
  • It has one more line only: "This part can be added to new work again."
  • An empty "Note (Optional)" box follows, then a white Cancel and a blue "Activate" button at the bottom right.
  • Behind the dialog the window's pill still reads "Inactive".

Step 5:

  • The confirmation closes and Edit Inventory Part shows again with Active still picked.

Step 6:

  • The window closes and part A is still listed on the Inactive tab.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change), story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S10-R3: “Raised from the bulk bar, the confirmation is titled "Deactivate parts?" or "Activate parts?". Raised from the part dialog, it is titled "Deactivate part?" or "Activate part?".”
  • S10-R4: “Raised from the bulk bar, the confirmation opens with "{n} parts selected.", or "1 part selected." for one. Raised from the part dialog, it opens with the part number followed by the description, as they stand in the form, with spaces before and after removed.”
  • S10-R7: “For a reactivation from the part dialog, the confirmation states "This part can be added to new work again." and nothing more.”
  • S10-R10: “The confirmation has a note field labelled "Note (Optional)". It stops accepting input at 255 characters.”
  • S10-R11: “The confirm button reads "Deactivate" in red for a deactivation and "Activate" in blue for a reactivation. Cancel sits to its left.”
  • S13-R25: “The title row pill shows the saved status, not the picked one.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "3.7 Bringing it back". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above where the PRD speaks, and from the board pictures where it is silent about the look.

The design also draws a grey close X at the right end of this confirmation's title row. Product confirmed on 27 Oct 2026 (answer 19) that the X stays and does what Cancel does (PRD v35, Key Decisions and S10-R11a); it is checked by the design case "Design: Status confirmation has a close X in its title row", so this case does not check it.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • retire-07-p3-7-activate-confirm.png

The design's own words:

  • “Active picked, then Save: "Activate part?", the part, then "This part can be added to new work again." and nothing more (S10-R7). The Activate button is blue (S10-R11).”
